label: Extended critique of postcolonial elite corruption to ecological sovereignty
description: Building on Fanon's warning against the postcolonial national bourgeoisie's extraction of public wealth, Maathai argued that forest grabbing, authoritarianism, and cultural alienation reproduce colonial exploitation from within.
dialecticalTension: Expands anti-colonial national liberation into living ecological stewardship.
historicalContext: Green Belt Movement struggle against the Moi regime (1977–2002).

label: Created the Green Belt framework uniting ecology, democracy, and peace
description: Maathai conceptualized the three-legged stool of environmental conservation, good governance, and culture of peace, demonstrating how planting indigenous trees builds democratic agency.
dialecticalTension: Dissolves false dichotomy between human survival needs and biodiversity restoration.

citations.author: Wangari Maathai
citations.work: Nobel Lecture & The Green Belt Movement

label: Pioneered Southern women's ecological commons praxis alongside Shiva's Chipko work
description: Maathai's Green Belt Movement (1977) formed a flagship African pillar of Global South ecofeminism that Vandana Shiva championed globally alongside India's Chipko forest movement.
dialecticalTension: Unites African land-regeneration praxis with South Asian anti-biopiracy philosophy.
